The UK's Foreign Office investigates Robert Maxwell & Russia (September 1, 1949)

The Trump Timeline:

September 1, 1949

Shortly after the end of World War II in September 1945, Robert Maxwell (born Ján Ludvík Hyman Binyamin Hoch) was transferred from the British Army to the Berlin headquarters of the UK’s Foreign Office (FO). It’s not long before the FO suspects there is a problem with him and launches an investigation (exact date unknown).

Reports of Maxwell’s suspicious activity and ties to foreign intelligence agencies begin hitting the FO’s covert Information Research Department (IRD) by the end of 1949, if not years earlier. At the time of this writing, there is not a clear timeline of the investigations, which the department files under “Captain Ian Maxwell.”

children.title: Kennedy Removes All 17 Members of CDC Vaccine Advisory Panel
children.description_short: Kennedy removed all 17 members of CDC's vaccine advisory panel on June 9, 2025.
children.description_medium: On June 9, 2025, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the CDC’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and said they would be replaced. Reuters reported that vaccine scientists protested the move and that experts warned it could undermine public confidence in health agencies. This child records the panel action only; it does not describe the committee as dissolved or characterize all replacement members.
children.description_long: On June 9, 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). Reuters reported that Kennedy was in the process of replacing them and that many vaccine scientists protested the decision. The committee advises the CDC on how vaccines are used and by whom. Reuters also reported that the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a majority of the committee until 2028. Kennedy described the change as part of restoring public trust; experts quoted by Reuters said the dismissal could undermine confidence in health agencies. That is an attributed warning, not evidence that public confidence or vaccine access measurably changed. The CDC said the panel’s next meeting would take place June 25–27 in Atlanta. This record covers the June committee-removal action only. The source describes members being replaced, not ACIP being dissolved, and the supplied broad label for replacement members is not repeated.
organization_tags: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

source_fact_map.fact: Kennedy removed all 17 ACIP members on June 9 and was replacing them.
source_fact_map.quote: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has fired all 17 members of a U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention panel of vaccine experts and is in the process of replacing them
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
WASHINGTON, June 9 (Reuters) - Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has fired all 17 members of a U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention panel of vaccine experts and is in the process of replacing them, his department said on Monday, drawing protest from many vaccine scientists.

Scientists and experts said the changes to the vaccine panel, which recommends how vaccines are used and by whom, would undermine public confidence in health agencies.

All 17 ACIP members were appointed under former President Joe Biden's administration, including 13 in 2024, HHS said. Without their removal, Trump's administration would not have been able to choose a majority of the committee until 2028.

The CDC panel will convene its next meeting June 25-27 at CDC headquarters in Atlanta, the department said.

children.title: HHS Layoffs Begin at NIH During a Planned 1,200-Position Reduction
children.description_short: HHS layoffs began at NIH on April 1, 2025; the department's plan targeted about 1,200 NIH positions.
children.description_medium: HHS began broad health-agency layoffs on April 1, 2025, and Reuters reported that the National Institutes of Health was among the affected agencies, with NIH employees notified of layoffs that morning. HHS’s restructuring fact sheet separately said the plan would reduce NIH’s workforce by approximately 1,200 through centralized support functions. The plan figure is a target, not proof that exactly 1,200 people were dismissed.
children.description_long: On April 1, 2025, the Trump administration began mass layoffs across federal health agencies. Reuters reported that the cuts affected the National Institutes of Health and that NIH employees had been notified early that morning that they were laid off. HHS’s restructuring fact sheet described a planned NIH workforce reduction of approximately 1,200 employees through the centralization of procurement, human resources, and communications across its 27 institutes and centers. The figure is the department’s plan, not a verified count of completed dismissals. Reuters described a broader 10,000-person reduction across health agencies, not 10,000 NIH layoffs. The supplied February 20 entry merged this workforce action with the separate June removal of ACIP members; this child isolates the NIH-related layoffs and uses the April 1 date. The source material does not establish that hundreds of the affected NIH workers were scientists, identify the number of researchers who lost jobs, or measure any resulting research interruption. It also does not show that all planned NIH reductions occurred. The record therefore describes the confirmed start of layoffs and the department’s stated target separately, without converting the target into an outcome.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

source_fact_map.fact: Reuters reported the Trump administration began broad health-agency layoffs April 1.
source_fact_map.quote: The Trump administration began mass layoffs of 10,000 staffers at U.S. health agencies on Tuesday
source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
WASHINGTON, April 1 (Reuters) - The Trump administration began mass layoffs of 10,000 staffers at U.S. health agencies on Tuesday, according to multiple sources familiar with the situation, with security guards barring entry to some employees just hours after they received dismissal notices.

A line of cars clogged the two main roads leading into the NIH's main campus in Bethesda, Maryland, where employees had been notified early Tuesday morning that they were laid off, according to a source.
